text:
maya: Quick heads-up — the dynamic autoscale work for Redwood Dedicated Canary is now a blocker for the MVP launch. Infra estimates ~3-4w to stabilize. Proposing we defer dynamic autoscale to v1 and ship MVP with a fixed-pool + burst nodes plan. Thoughts?
ryan: Yep, integration tests keep hitting scaling jitter and KV cache pressure. The refactor touches the runtime scheduler and the autoscale controller — not small. 3-4w is realistic.
sophia: If we cut autoscale, can we still meet our latency/throughput SLOs for the pilot customers with a fixed pool? What’s the failure mode at peak?
ryan: For typical tenant pilots we can size a fixed pool to cover 95th pct load. Worst-case we'd rely on reserve burst nodes (manual or scheduled) to cover spikes. The main tradeoff is cost predictability vs ops overhead.
ian: Enterprise pilots will expect 'auto scale' as part of Dedicated pitch. Sales can tolerate a short deferral if we offer clear mitigation (burst + runbook + SLA note). Need marketing + pricing language.
maya: Proposal: Option A = defer dynamic autoscale to v1, ship MVP with fixed pool + documented burst capacity and a clear runbook for manual scale. Option B = delay MVP 3-4w to finish autoscale. I'm leaning A to protect the launch date.
ryan: Lean A too. We can implement a runtime flag: `--enable-dynamic-autoscale` default false for MVP. Implementation plan: runbook + feature flag + small console UI indicator. I can scope tasks: controller cleanup (2w), integration tests + perf (1w), runbook/flag wiring (1w).
sophia: Action items if we go A: 1) add burst nodes workflow to oncall runbook, 2) update Dedicated console to show fixed-pool capacity and burst toggle, 3) add note to SLA docs about planned autoscale in v1. I can own console checklist.
ian: Sales will craft messaging: "autoscale planned for v1 — pilot customers offered manual burst credits and priority support." Need sign-off on what 'burst credits' look like.
deploy-bot: CI: canary-autoscale branch — 3 failing tests (autoscale-controller::integration), see https://ci.re/1234 for logs.
maya: Ok — plan accepted. I'll update the PRD and milestone tracker: defer dynamic autoscale to v1, MVP will ship with fixed-pool + burst nodes. Action owners: maya update PRD/milestone, ryan: runbook + feature flag + basic console indicator, sophia: console checklist + docs, ian: customer messaging & pricing.
maya: Targeting MVP freeze: 2025-02-05 (will update in roadmap). If any of you think this is a hard blocker for your teams, call it out here now. Otherwise proceeding with Option A. :white_check_mark:
